title: Emergency stop and interlocks
summary: Make a running line stop when the emergency stop is pressed, show it with the red light and refuse to restart until Start is pressed again.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Stop every output while the emergency stop is pressed.
Remember the stop, so that releasing the button does not restart the line.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The starting program in src/ThreeLevelLifts.st runs the line and has no stop. While the emergency stop is pressed, every belt and lift must be off and the red lamp lit; the line must stay stopped when the button is released and run again only after a new press of Start.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which outputs must be off during the stop, what Red must show, and what must still be true after the button is released.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the stop: at 15.5 s the emergency stop is pressed while a lift may be moving; the line must stop, stay stopped when the button is released at 17 s, and run again only after the Start press at 17.5 s.
stages.checkpoint: Red on and every output off at 16 s; still stopped at 17.3 s; Red off and the line running again after Start.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter ignores the emergency stop: at 16 s, with it pressed, the line keeps running and Red stays off. While EStopOk is FALSE, every output must be off and Red lit; after the release the line must stay stopped and run again only with a new press of Start.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named estop-interlocks and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the stack light turn red and the belts and lifts stop when the scenario presses the emergency stop, and run again after Start.
stages.checkpoint: Red stays on after the release until Start, and the outputs fall in the same scan as EStopOk.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The AT assertions pin the stop at 16 s, the held stop at 17.3 s and Red off at 18 s; the interlocks that were already in the program are the same idea as in the 2.0 lesson interlock-guard-permissive.
stages.checkpoint: This stop is only what the program does with the EStopOk signal: it is not an emergency-stop circuit and it gives no stopping time. The grade cannot see a lift that keeps rising a little after the stop.

hints.text: Look at 17.3 s, after the button is released: EStopOk is TRUE again, yet Red is still lit and the outputs are still off. Which variable of your program can say that, and what makes it change?

Declare Stopped : BOOL in VAR. Replace the start lines at the top with IF NOT EStopOk THEN Stopped := TRUE; Active := FALSE; ELSIF Start THEN Stopped := FALSE; Active := TRUE; END_IF; and replace Red := FALSE with Red := Stopped;. Every output already depends on Active, so no output needs its own stop logic.

faultCases: The starter ignores the emergency stop: at 16 s, with it pressed, the line keeps running and Red stays off.
